title: Etale at a prime iff flat and unramified at that prime (finitely presented)
statement: Let R\to S be a ring map making S a finitely presented R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let q be a prime of S and p=q\cap R. The following are equivalent: (1) Algebra.IsEtaleAt R q, that is, the localization S_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is formally etale over R; (2) there is g\in S\setminus q such that \operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}R is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; (3) S_q is flat over R_p [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and the localization (\Omega_{S/R})_q of the module of Kahler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is zero.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00U6 (lemma-characterize-etale, line 39470) with lemma-unramified-at-prime and Tag 08WD (lemma-etale-flat-unramified-finite-presentation, line 41644): pointwise characterization of etale at a prime

proof.text: Apply the localized cotangent criterion [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-formally-etale-cotangent-criterion] to Algebra.IsEtaleAt R q: it gives H_1(L_{S/R})_q=0 and (Omega_{S/R})_q=0. Since S is a finitely presented R-algebra, the etale-near-prime lemma [lem-weil-pbc-etale-near-prime-naive-cotangent-vanishing] (with A=R, C=S) then gives g in S\q such that the affine scheme map Spec(S_g) \to Spec(R) is etale, proving (1) implies (2).

Assume (2). The affine etale ring-map criterion [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] gives H_1(L_{S_g/R})=0 and Omega_{S_g/R}=0. Localizing these zero modules at the prime induced by q gives the two vanishings required by [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-formally-etale-cotangent-criterion]; the identity (S_g)_{qS_g}=S_q is the defining localization identity. Hence S_q is formally etale over R, so (1) holds.

Assume (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], S_g is flat over R. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] with A=S_g, W the complement of qS_g, A'=(S_g)_{qS_g}=S_q and M=S_q: M is free, hence flat, over A', so S_q is flat over S_g. A flat module over a flat algebra is flat over the base (tensor associativity, Stacks Tag 00HC), so S_q is flat over R. Elements of R\setminus p map to units of S_q, so S_q is an R_p-module; applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] to R\to R_p with M=S_q gives that S_q is flat over R_p. The vanishing Omega_{S_g/R}=0 from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] localizes to (Omega_{S/R})_q=0, since (Omega_{S/R})_g=Omega_{S_g/R} (Stacks Tag 00RT) and S_q is a localization of S_g. Thus (3) holds.

source.place: Lemma 08WD and the localization clause for differentials

proof.text: Assume (3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness] to M=S. Its flat locus contains q, so choose g1 not in q such that every localization S_{q'} for q' in Spec(S_{g1}) is flat over R. After localizing the base, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] gives flatness over each corresponding R_{q' cap R}; then [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base] gives S_{g1} flat over R. Since S is finitely presented, Omega_{S/R} is finitely generated; the vanishing at q in (3) therefore gives g2 not in q with (Omega_{S/R})_{g2}=0. Put g=g1g2. Then Spec(S_g)\to Spec(R) is flat, and [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] identifies the vanishing of Omega_{S_g/R} with unramifiedness. It is locally of finite presentation because S is finitely presented, so [def-weil-etale-morphism] makes Spec(S_g)\to Spec(R) etale. This proves (2).
